classification.difficultyReason: Apply triangle and quadrilateral angle sums, including a two-triangle figure and exterior angles, with reasons.

content.prompt: This question reviews angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals. Find the angles marked with pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A above BC; all three interior angle labels retained.
spec.mathematics: Angle A is theta, angle B is 80 degrees and angle C is 65 degrees.

answer.worked:
The angles of $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta+80^\circ+65^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Quadrilateral KLMN with coordinate-derived right-angle squares at K and M.
spec.mathematics: Angles K and M are 90 degrees, L is 115 degrees and N is alpha.

answer.worked:
The angles of quadrilateral $KLMN$ sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+90^\circ+115^\circ+90^\circ&=360^\circ\\\alpha&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: P, A and B are collinear. A curved leader identifies the narrow interior angle ACB as 20 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angle PAC is theta; interior ABC is 110 degrees and ACB is 20 degrees.

answer.worked:
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles of $\triangle ABC$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=110^\circ+20^\circ\\\theta&=130^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Quadrilateral RSTU and diagonal US, retaining the curved 50-degree leader to the upper angle RUS.
spec.mathematics: URS=110 degrees, RUS=50 degrees, SUT=UST=40 degrees, RSU=alpha and STU=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens retained; unknowns remain alpha and beta.

answer.short:
$\alpha=20^\circ$, $\beta=100^\circ$.

Use the angle sum in each of $\triangle URS$ and $\triangle UST$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle URS$, the angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+110^\circ+50^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle UST$, the angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta+40^\circ+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded irregular quadrilateral FEHG with each interior angle label retained.
spec.mathematics: F=2theta, E=130 degrees, H=80 degrees and G=theta.

answer.worked:
The angles of quadrilateral $FEHG$ sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}2\theta+130^\circ+80^\circ+\theta&=360^\circ\\3\theta+210^\circ&=360^\circ\\3\theta&=150^\circ\\\theta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal A-B-C and perpendicular vertical B-D-E-F, with separate segments AD and CE. All six point labels and the redundant 140-degree given retained.
spec.mathematics: BAD=45 degrees, ABD=90 degrees, ADE=beta and CEF=140 degrees.

answer.worked:
Since $AB\perp BD$, $\angle ABD=90^\circ$. The exterior angle of $\triangle ABD$ equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=45^\circ+90^\circ\\\beta&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$
